articles.title: Real Madrid demand immediate Tebas resignation over ‘morally repugnant’ Goebbels comparison
articles.summary: The club have been left furious by remarks Tebas made on social media.
articles.content:
Real Madrid demand immediate Tebas resignation over ‘morally repugnant’ Goebbels comparison

The club have been left furious by remarks Tebas made on social media.

Last Update:

Real Madrid have demanded the immediate resignation of LaLiga president Javier Tebas after he compared the club’s communication strategy to that of Joseph Goebbels.

Tebas made the comments in a lengthy social media post on Friday, likening the approach of Madrid’s hierarchy and the management of their in-house TV channel to the techniques employed by the Nazi propaganda minister.

He wrote: “Real Madrid’s management directs an orchestra of mouthpieces and Real Madrid TV leads the singing.“Their score is always the same: select the plays that suit them, repeat the grievance, feed the suspicion, and point fingers at the enemies.

“That method recalls propaganda mechanisms exploited by Goebbels, Nazi Germany’s minister of propaganda: systematic repetition, construction of an enemy, and subordination of facts to the narrative.”

Tebas insisted he was simply comparing the “propaganda techniques” and “not with an ideology”.

But his remarks have predictably left Madrid furious, with the club making clear their belief that the comments should disqualify Tebas from holding his position as the boss of LaLiga and as vice-president of the Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF).

A statement from Madrid read: “In response to the statements made by Javier Tebas, president of LaLiga and vice president of the Royal Spanish Football Federation, in which he compares the methods of the Real Madrid management to those employed by Joseph Goebbels, the Minister of Propaganda of the Nazi regime, and points to Real Madrid TV as an instrument of this alleged strategy, Real Madrid C. F. declares the following:

“Real Madrid C. F. considers it absolutely intolerable and extraordinarily serious that someone holding two positions of utmost responsibility in Spanish football resorts to a comparison with the propaganda methods of the Nazi regime to discredit our club, its management, and its television. The clarification that he is not referring to Nazi ideology does not mitigate the deeply offensive, morally repugnant, and institutionally unworthy nature of his statements.

“These statements constitute yet another episode in the repeated attacks by Javier Tebas against Real Madrid, its president, and its media outlets. It is unacceptable that he even takes advantage of questions, information, or opinions from journalists unrelated to the club to direct his accusations at us, attributing to us actions of third parties for which we bear no responsibility.“It is especially concerning that Tebas uses these statements to question the legitimate actions of Real Madrid and Real Madrid TV in relation to the Negreira case.“In light of the lack of response to the extraordinary seriousness of the Negreira case by the two institutions where Javier Tebas holds positions of utmost relevance, our club has had to approach UEFA directly to demand a full clarification of the payments made over the years by F. C. Barcelona to the vice president of the Technical Committee of Referees and the adoption of necessary measures to ensure the integrity of competitions.“Real Madrid also demands a comprehensive overhaul of the refereeing system and the federative structures of governance, management, supervision, and discipline, through the renewal of those who held positions of responsibility during that period.“It is particularly significant that Javier Tebas, president of LaLiga and vice president of the Royal Spanish Football Federation, an organization that includes the Technical Committee of Referees, dedicates his efforts to discrediting Real Madrid instead of promoting, from his institutional responsibilities, the clarification of these extremely serious events and the necessary regeneration of Spanish football.“Javier Tebas’s repeated conduct demonstrates a lack of neutrality, respect, and impartiality incompatible with his institutional responsibilities. His constant attacks on Real Madrid and those demanding transparency and regeneration represent, in our club’s view, a genuine scourge for Spanish football.“For all these reasons, Real Madrid C. F. considers that the repeated statements and behaviors of Javier Tebas would be unacceptable in any European sports institution governed by principles of respect, neutrality, and integrity, and that they disqualify him institutionally from continuing to hold the positions he occupies.

“Consequently, Real Madrid C. F. demands his immediate resignation as president of LaLiga and vice president of the Royal Spanish Football Federation.

“Real Madrid C. F. will continue to defend its rights, its institutional prestige, the full clarification of the Negreira case, and the necessary regeneration of Spanish football.”

articles.title: Chelsea: Alonso offers no timeline for James return amid reports of three-month lay-off
articles.summary: Another long spell on the sidelines awaits the Chelsea skipper.
articles.content:
Chelsea: Alonso offers no timeline for James return amid reports of three-month lay-off

Another long spell on the sidelines awaits the Chelsea skipper.

Last Update:

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso expressed his disappointment at captain Reece James’ latest injury setback, which has reportedly left him facing a three-month lay-off.

The Blues confirmed on Friday that James had undergone minor knee surgery on an injury suffered in training ahead of last week’s 5-1 win over Bournemouth.

While the club did not give a timeline for his return, subsequent reports have claimed the England right-back faces another elongated spell on the sidelines.

And, though he also did not offer a timescale for James’ recovery, Alonso indicated it will indeed be an extended absence for the 26-year-old.

Speaking ahead of Saturday’s Premier League clash with Everton, Alonso said: “We are all disappointed, especially for him. He wanted to have a good start after the international break, but he picked up an injury.

“The surgery has been successful. We are supporting him.

“I wish him the best recovery. We won’t set timelines, but we expect him to be out for several weeks.

“It’s not going to be short. Whether it’s before or after Christmas then time will tell. It needs to be done properly.

“We have a big squad to deal with injuries.We have four more games until the next break so I think we can manage well with the players that we have.”

Asked if Chelsea might need to sign cover for James in the January transfer window, Alonso replied: “I don’t think so, we expect by that time he will be back. It doesn’t affect [that].

“He is still a very important player. He is the captain, he is a great influence and hopefully after he recovers from this injury he will be available for many games.

“He has a good mentality and we need him.”

In addition to losing his versatility in being able to play right-back and in midfield, James’ absence also leaves a leadership void in the Chelsea team.

But Alonso has two leading candidates to take that role, adding: “We have Moi [Moises Caicedo], Levi [Colwill], we have players who take the responsibility and take the role in a perfect way.

“They have the support from the rest when they see them with the armband, so it is no bother.”

articles.title: Carrick: Man United have moved on from Martinez saga
articles.summary: Martinez will be in the squad for United's trip to Leeds on Sunday.
articles.content:
Carrick: Man United have moved on from Martinez saga

Martinez will be in the squad for United's trip to Leeds on Sunday.

Last Update:

Michael Carrick insists Manchester United have moved on from the saga surrounding Lisandro Martinez’s comments in the wake of their Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid.

Martinez questioned United’s summer transfer business and technical director Jason Wilcox after Tuesday’s 2-0 Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid.

The Argentine defender subsequently claimed his comments had come from “anger and frustration” and, having issued an apology, was reported to have been fined by the club.

With Carrick under significant pressure following United’s worst start to a top-flight season since 1986, the episode could hardly have come at a worse time.

United visit Leeds United on Sunday in what is likely to be a hugely difficult encounter at Elland Road.

But, speaking in his pre-match press conference, Carrick was adamant spirits are high in the United camp.

“It’s done really,” Carrick said when asked about the Martinez saga.

“We’ve moved on from that. It was one of those things. He has come out and acknowledged the situation and as a group we have moved on.

“It is really not a drama for us as a group. The boys have trained really well, there was a really good feeling around training this morning. Really good feeling.

“From the outside [you are] after some big information about big discussions but it was pretty simple. We all understood the situation and what it meant. He made his statement and acknowledges that it was a mistake from him and that was it really.

“We have a really good feeling from within the group. We have a really good feeling within the club from the inside.

“Results-wise it hasn’t gone to plan of late but the spirit, the togetherness, again I said it but today was one of the better training sessions that we have had and you can see there’s a real sense and a feeling within the group that we want to do something about this situation and want to do something about it quickly.

“We understand the situation that came up after the game but we feel that has been dealt with and we have moved on.

“Genuinely moved on and there’s a freshness about the group today which I really liked.”

Carrick confirmed Martinez will be in the squad to face Leeds, but Luke Shaw and Kobbie Mainoo remain doubts, while Benjamin Sesko will once again miss out.

“We will see on Luke Shaw and Kobbie Mainoo,” Carrick added. “Ben is still undergoing a couple of checks before we update on timelines.

“We are trying to be clear what that looks like. He is still a little bit further away but when we know a bit more we will let you know.”

articles.title: Bellingham reportedly agrees new long-term Madrid contract
articles.summary: Bellingham is set to extend his deal until 2031.
articles.content:
Bellingham reportedly agrees new long-term Madrid contract

Bellingham is set to extend his deal until 2031.

Last Update:

Jude Bellingham has reportedly agreed a new long-term contract with Real Madrid.

AS reported on Friday that Bellingham, whose current deal is due to expire at the end of the 2028-29 season, is set to sign fresh terms to keep him at the Santiago Bernabeu until June 2031.

The England star will receive improved terms that are reflective of his importance to the team and the reputation he has in the Madrid changing room.

Bellingham has made 150 appearances for Madrid since joining from Borussia Dortmund in 2023.

He won LaLiga and the Champions League in his first season at the club, and has also lifted the Supercopa de Espana, UEFA Super Cup and FIFA Intercontinental Cup.

The 23-year-old has scored 49 goals for Madrid, his last coming in September against Rayo Vallecano.

Bellingham will have another chance to reach his half-century when Madrid face Sevilla on Sunday.

articles.title: Kompany confirms Neuer doubt as Bayern prepare for Leipzig test
articles.summary: The veteran goalkeeper missed Bayern's Champions League draw with Viking.
articles.content:
Kompany confirms Neuer doubt as Bayern prepare for Leipzig test

The veteran goalkeeper missed Bayern's Champions League draw with Viking.

Last Update:

Bayern Munich goalkeeper Manuel Neuer could be facing a spell on the sidelines due to a foot injury.

The 40-year-old missed Bayern’s 3-3 Champions League draw with Viking in midweek, and coach Vincent Kompany revealed the veteran was absent from training on Thursday as Bayern prepare to face RB Leipzig in the Bundesliga.

“Manu did not train yesterday. That means we have to see today how he feels and what the situation is like there,” Kompany told his pre-match press conference.

“We don’t have more information today. I don’t want to take on the role of a doctor. It’s on the foot, not on the thigh or the shoulder.

“It won’t take that long. Whether it’s tomorrow or next week, we’ll see. He should first get a better feeling and train when he can, then this phase will be over again.”

Defending Bundesliga champions Bayern are two points behind Freiburg and Borussia Dortmund at the top of the table.

An error by Neuer saw Bayern concede the fastest goal in Bundesliga history last week in a 3-3 draw at Augsburg.

Jonas Urbig played in goal against Viking, though Sven Ulreich is also an option in Neuer’s potential absence.

Despite the results against Augsburg and Viking, Kompany believes Bayern are not far from their best as they face a Leipzig side just two points behind them in the table and coming off a 1-0 win over PSV Eindhoven in the Champions League.

“We want to attack,” Kompany said. “We have ​the feeling that there are a lot of things behind the perception of these two results. I have ⁠the feeling it ​is just before we show our very best version.

“In the last two matches we shot 50 times on goal. If we do a few things better then we ‌are not too far from our very best version.

“These moments that some people think might be difficult we say these ‌are the best moments you can have in your ​career. If you win these matches then you ‌have created some moments.

“We are sharp and motivated. We look forward to these matches to measure ourselves against the best.

“The lads reach the limit in every training session and it is fun ⁠to watch. They know it ⁠is now best ‌to talk on the pitch.”

articles.title: Getafe president confirms talks to sign Sancho
articles.summary: Sancho remains without a club following the end of his time at Old Trafford.
articles.content:
Getafe president confirms talks to sign Sancho

Sancho remains without a club following the end of his time at Old Trafford.

Last Update:

Getafe‘s president has confirmed the LaLiga club are in talks to sign former Manchester United winger Jadon Sancho.

Sancho has been without a club since his contract at Old Trafford expired this summer, having spent the 2025-26 season on loan at Aston Villa, with whom he won the Europa League.

The 26-year-old previously had loan spells with Chelsea in 2024-25 and Borussia Dortmund in 2023-24. Neither spell proved successful, with Sancho failing to hit the heights he reached during his first spell with Dortmund, which convinced United to make an ill-fated £73million move to secure his services.

Having reportedly turned down a move to Russian side Krasnodar, Sancho may now be bound for Spain, with Getafe president Angel Torres confirming the talks prior to their Conference League clash with Craiova.

He told Movistar Plus: “We are in talks with Sancho, just as we were three or four months ago.

“[Dani] Parejo could also be another option. We should be able to confirm whether or not we finalise these negotiations next week.”

Getafe have taken eight points from their opening eight LaLiga games and sit 14th in the table. They host fellow Madrid side Rayo Vallecano on Monday.

articles.title: Chelsea captain James undergoes knee surgery
articles.summary: No timeframe has been given for James' return.
articles.content:
Chelsea captain James undergoes knee surgery

No timeframe has been given for James' return.

Last Update:

Chelsea captain Reece James has undergone surgery on a knee injury.

The club announced on Friday that James, who has regularly dealt with injury issues in his career, had a successful “minor” procedure.

England defender James suffered the injury in training and was forced to miss Chelsea’s 5-1 win over Bournemouth last Saturday, with surgery deemed the best course of action.

Chelsea’s statement read in part: “Reece has already begun his road to recovery and will be supported by the club’s medical department at Cobham during this rehabilitation phase.”

The club did not give a timeframe for the versatile right-back’s return.

His absence further limits Chelsea’s options in midfield, where James has played regularly in recent times.

While Chelsea have Marco Palestra and Malo Gusto to fill the void at right-back, James’ injury leaves them with only four senior options in central midfield in the form of Moises Caicedo, Jordan Henderson, Romeo Lavia and Valentin Barco.

Xabi Alonso’s men face Everton in Saturday’s early Premier League kick-off. A win would at least temporarily move Chelsea into the top four.

Tip of the Day: Wolves to get back on track, Deportivo to continue fine LaLiga start

After success with our selections in the Europa League, attention turns back to domestic competitions. Friday's Tip of the Day is here...

Last Update:

Another day, another win. Our Europa League treble on Thursday delivered the goods and we are four from four for the week on Tip of the Day.

No pressure then, heading into Friday.

With continental competitions in the books for another week, it’s time to turn attention back to the domestic leagues.

There’s a cracker in Championship between two sides relegated from the Premier League last season, and some enticing offerings in Spain and Germany among the fixtures on Friday.

As it’s Friday, why not go big? We’ve identified a three-leg acca with both teams to score in each game that offers a huge payout.

In the Championship, Burnley have enjoyed a resurgence of late after a dreadful start. They are unbeaten in their last three games, however, they have only kept one clean sheet in that run.

Hoping to take advantage of that lack of defensive solidity will be Wolves, who have slipped down the table of late following defeats to Middlesbrough and Bolton Wanderers. However, they have the edge in terms of quality and we’re going with Cesar Peixoto’s men to take all three points.

In Spain, Deportivo La Coruna have enjoyed an excellent start to life back in LaLiga, taking 10 points from eight games. They have lost only once in four home games, so we’re going with them to at least temporarily move into the top six with a win over a struggling Levante side that drew 3-3 with Sevilla last time out.

For a final selection we’re heading to the Bundesliga, in which Eintracht Frankfurt and Cologne kick off the weekend.

Cologne have yet to win away from home this season. We expect that run to continue but, against an Eintracht side that has already shipped 16 this season, we think the visitors will at least get a goal.

articles.title: Milan teenager Cisse makes history with hat-trick as Juve leave it late at Celta Vigo
articles.summary: Cisse made Italian football history for the Rossoneri.
articles.content:
Milan teenager Cisse makes history with hat-trick as Juve leave it late at Celta Vigo

Cisse made Italian football history for the Rossoneri.

Last Update:

AC Milan got off the mark in the Europa League in style as they cruised to a 4-0 win at Red Bull Salzburg thanks to a hat-trick from Alphadjo Cisse.

The teenager was the star of the show in Austria, becoming the youngest Italian to score a treble in a European competition, doing so at the age of 19 years and 358 days.

Goncalo Ramos was also on target for the Rossoneri, who had Filippo Terracciano sent off late on as they bounced back from defeat to Benfica in their league phase opener.

Their Serie A rivals Juventus made it two wins from two as they came from behind to beat Celta Vigo 2-1.

Nick Woltemade equalised for Juve after Hugo Alvarez had given the hosts the lead, the striker on loan from Newcastle United pouncing on poor defending to fire home his second goal for the club.

Juve completed the turnaround in stoppage time, Randal Kolo Muani heading home from Andrea Cambiaso’s superb cross.

There were mixed fortunes for the Premier League teams. Sunderland needed a stoppage-time winner to beat Portuguese second-tier side Torreense 2-1, while Bournemouth were more comfortable in seeing off Sturm Graz 3-0. Crystal Palace failed to make it a clean sweep for English sides, though, as they lost 3-2 at Lyon.

Scottish champions Celtic lost 4-1 at Benfica, and there was a similarly emphatic scoreline in Poland as Lech Poznan were beaten 4-0 at home by Bayer Leverkusen.

Hoffenheim’s miserable start to the season continued as they were beaten 3-2 at home by Besiktas, leaving the Bundesliga side still without a point in the competition. Marseille are also pointless after a 1-0 defeat at home to Olympiacos.

Their Ligue 1 rivals Rennes came from behind to beat OFI Crete 2-1, Abdelhamid Ait Boudlal scoring a 90th-minute winner. There was also late drama in Croatia as Dion Beljo’s 96th-minute penalty gave Dinamo Zagreb a 1-0 win over Anderlecht.

Elsewhere, Real Sociedad claimed their first point as they drew 1-1 with Union Saint-Gilloise.

Paris the star for Monaco

Paris Brunner scored Monaco’s first and provided the assist for Ansu Fati for their second as the Ligue 1 side opened their Conference League campaign with a 2-1 win at CSKA Sofia.

Atalanta, meanwhile, scored three first-half goals to cruise to a 3-1 win over Pafos in a meeting of two sides who played Champions League football last term, while Brighton and Hove Albion were 4-0 winners over Kauno Zalgiris.

Mohamed Salah was on target as Trabzonspor won 4-2 at KuPS, but there was disappointment for Dutch giants Ajax, who suffered a 2-1 defeat at Hajduk Split.

Last season’s Europa League finalists Freiburg beat Jablonec 3-2, while Copenhagen produced one of the most impressive results of the opening round of Conference League games, defeating Braga 3-0.

articles.title: Lewis Cook hails ‘special night’ as Bournemouth maintain perfect Europa League start
articles.summary: Bournemouth were in top form as they dispatched Sturm Graz in the Europa League.
articles.content:
Lewis Cook hails ‘special night’ as Bournemouth maintain perfect Europa League start

Bournemouth were in top form as they dispatched Sturm Graz in the Europa League.

Last Update:

Bournemouth midfielder Lewis Cook praised his side’s performance after the Cherries continued their perfect start to the Europa League with a win over Sturm Graz.

The result made it two wins from two in Europe for Bournemouth, who responded to Saturday’s Premier League defeat at Chelsea with an impressive display.

Cook was particularly pleased with the atmosphere and the way his team-mates handled the occasion, describing it as a night the club could be proud of.

Speaking to TNT Sports after the match, Cook praised the collective effort and admitted the occasion felt special even before kick-off.

“I thought the performance was top. It was a special night, you could feel that before the game, when were lining up as players,” he said.

“The atmosphere was great. It was a top performance, we bounced back from the weekend and it was something we can be very proud of.”

Bournemouth had little time to dwell on their defeat at Stamford Bridge, with their European commitments offering an immediate opportunity to respond.

Cook believes the quick turnaround helped the squad move on from that disappointment and produce a much-improved performance.

“That is a positive. There are so many games in a short space of time,” he explained.

“If we have a bad game then we’ve only got a couple of days to get over it and then onto the next one and I thought the lads showed that today and handled themselves well.

“It is tough with a bad result to come back and do well. Everyone who played today was fantastic and it was a collective effort and a great win.”

articles.title: Regis Le Bris hails ‘special’ Sunderland win as Black Cats win again on European return
articles.summary: Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris has hailed his team after their win in Europe.
articles.content:
Regis Le Bris hails ‘special’ Sunderland win as Black Cats win again on European return

Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris has hailed his team after their win in Europe.

Last Update:

Sunderland manager Regis Le Bris hailed a “very special” night for the club after the Black Cats continued their return to European football with a dramatic late win.

Sunderland left it until the closing stages to secure the three points, sparking wild celebrations among their travelling supporters.

Le Bris praised his young squad for showing the belief to keep pushing until the final whistle, insisting the experience would prove valuable as they continue to develop.

“We’re back in Europe 53 years later and winning this game right at the end is very special,” Le Bris said.

“It is a symbol, and important, I think for many reasons. The first one is for our club and our fans, they were fantastic once again.

“Also we are growing up and we need experiences, and I think the team showed this belief until the very end. It is important for us to show this mindset.”

The Sunderland boss also highlighted the youthfulness of his squad, revealing that the average age of his starting XI was just over 22.

“Absolutely. The starting 11 was 22 point something this evening, which shows that this team is young with huge potential, but potential is about getting experience to learn and grow.

“Sometimes it’s tough, you have to expect that. Showing consistency and discipline.”

Le Bris also reserved praise for Noah Sadiki, who got on the scoresheet during the contest.

The midfielder’s attacking contribution particularly pleased his manager, who believes he has the qualities to become an even greater threat in the final third.

“It’s important for him to step up and add this layer to his game because he has the ability to hit the box, to dribble, to shout to make key passes.

“Now it’s the next layer, so I hope it’s a starting point.”

articles.title: Newcastle boss Jaissle backs ‘amazing’ Fernandez-Pardo after Coventry struggles
articles.summary: The £51m signing has yet to score for Newcastle.
articles.content:
Newcastle boss Jaissle backs ‘amazing’ Fernandez-Pardo after Coventry struggles

The £51m signing has yet to score for Newcastle.

Last Update:

Matthias Jaissle praised Matias Fernandez-Pardo as an “amazing player” despite the Newcastle United forward’s struggles in front of goal against Coventry City.

Newcastle’s first game back following the international break proved a chastening one as they lost 4-1 to newly promoted Coventry City.

The Magpies dominated possession and had 19 shots on goal, but were guilty of a series of errors in their own box and a lack of precision in the final third as they missed the opportunity to go fourth in the Premier League.

Fernandez-Pardo, a £51million signing from Lille on transfer deadline day, produced a profligate display as he waits for his first goal for the club.

The Belgium international inexplicably dummied a Jacob Murphy near-post cross instead of going for goal with Newcastle in the ascendancy at 1-0 down, and then saw two potential equalisers cleared off the line by Coventry defender Bobby Thomas.

Jaissle: Newcastle forward needs goal for confidence

But Jaissle, who himself has been the subject of criticism in the wake of a hugely disappointing result, was encouraged by Fernandez-Pardo’s success in getting into positions for shots on goal.

“Young lads coming to the Premier League for the first time need that adaptation time. I got advice that I should be patient at least half a year with them,” Jaissle told a pre-match press conference ahead of Saturday’s meeting with Aston Villa.

“Of course, you don’t have the time in the Premier League so the development and adjustment needs to be as fast as possible.

“I’m glad we’re already seeing him in the situations that’s he bringing the principles on the pitch. He’s creating the chances and I think it’s just a goal missing to give him the confidence back. He’s an amazing player and he has so much potential.”

Newcastle received good news on the injury front, with Bazoumana Toure expected to be in the squad for the Villa game despite the Ivorian going off with an injury late on against Coventry.

Jaissle indicated midfielder Joelinton will be fit enough to start after coming off the bench on Monday, though it is likely to be too soon for captain Dan Burn to do the same.

Anthony Elanga (hamstring) and Jacob Ramsey (thigh) are set to return to training next week, though Newcastle are being more cautious with right-back Tino Livramento, who missed the win over Hull City before the international break and has not returned having pulled out of the England camp for their UEFA Nations League matches.

On Elanga, Jaissle said: “Unfortunately, he’s been out for many, many weeks. Now, it’s the process is to bring back him back slowly but surely in a smart way and not too much in a hurry.

“Hopefully, next week, he is about to train again with the group, at least partially and we then integrate him again step-by-step. We miss him a lot. I can’t wait to have him back in the squad.

“With Tino, we need to be cautious and we don’t rush him. We know about his injury situation and history but we’re optimistic in the next few weeks we can bring him back step by step.

“With JJ, it’s a bit different. He’s making progress. Hopefully next week, he can join in partially in training and then we can build it from there.”

articles.summary: Gianni Infantino has been told he is not 'fit to lead' FIFA.
articles.content:
FIFA president Gianni Infantino warned he is ‘not fit to lead’ despite apology over World Cup sell-off plan

Gianni Infantino has been told he is not 'fit to lead' FIFA.

Last Update:

FIFA president Gianni Infantino has apologised to the organisation’s Council over his controversial World Cup sell-off proposal, but has been warned he is “not fit” to lead unless he answers outstanding questions.

Infantino faced criticism during a three-and-a-half-hour meeting in Zurich on Thursday, the first gathering of the FIFA Council since details of his secret FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan emerged.

The proposal, which was abandoned within days of becoming public, would have handed a portion of FIFA’s commercial rights to a private investment firm.

However, Football Association chair and FIFA vice-president Debbie Hewitt insisted Infantino’s apology was not enough, demanding the release of documents relating to the project.

Infantino warned he is ‘not fit’ to lead FIFA

Hewitt described Thursday’s discussions as the “most robust, most frank, most open Council meeting” she had experienced, but expressed frustration that several important questions remained unanswered.

“One of the disappointing things is that we didn’t get answers to anything that we had specifically requested – for example getting the papers from FFE,” she said.

“I asked the question ‘why not?’ – and we were asked to submit those questions in writing.

“I think the man has to answer those questions and if he doesn’t answer those questions now, he’s not fit to be Fifa president – and that was what was shared in the meeting.

“What he really apologised for was not bringing it to the Council. If you regret it that deeply, share it with us,” she added.

The FA chair also demanded explanations surrounding the suspended red-card ban handed to United States striker Folarin Balogun during the World Cup and the FIFA Peace Prize.

“The responses to those questions, which I still don’t have answers to, will determine from my personal point of view whether or not Gianni is the right candidate,” she said.

UEFA maintains pressure on Infantino over FFE controversy

UEFA has been among Infantino’s strongest critics since the FFE proposal emerged, repeatedly calling for the FIFA president to resign.

European football’s governing body has prepared criminal legal proceedings against Infantino and lodged claims in three US courts seeking the release of documents connected to the abandoned project.

Hewitt believes the FIFA Council must be given access to those papers before determining whether further action is necessary.

“Those papers coming to Council are a crucial next part of us feeling comfortable as to what, if any, criminal proceedings need to take place,” she said.

“From my position, nothing has shifted. I’ve no new information that makes me feel any differently, other than we do have a president who is apologetic.”

articles.title: Roy Keane slams Manchester United as ‘a circus’ after Lisandro Martinez’s attack on club hierarchy
articles.summary: Roy Keane has criticised Manchester United's Lisandro Martinez for his comments in midweek.
articles.content:
Roy Keane slams Manchester United as ‘a circus’ after Lisandro Martinez’s attack on club hierarchy

Roy Keane has criticised Manchester United's Lisandro Martinez for his comments in midweek.

Last Update:

Roy Keane has described Manchester United as “a bit of a circus” following Lisandro Martinez’s public criticism of the club’s hierarchy.

Martinez questioned United’s summer transfer business and technical director Jason Wilcox after Tuesday’s 2-0 Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid.

The Argentine defender subsequently claimed his comments had come from “anger and frustration”, but Keane believes the outburst reflects the problems currently facing the club.

United are without a win in five matches and have managed just one Premier League win from their opening six games of the season.

Speaking on The Overlap podcast, Keane criticised Martinez for publicly questioning the club’s leadership when his own performances have come under scrutiny.

“There will be some fans saying it’s great and some saying you’re letting the team down, especially from a player who hasn’t been at his best, when the team is struggling,” Keane said.

“I think as a reflection of the club, it’s obviously chaos there, like a bit of a circus.

“When you’re going through a difficult spell like United are, the issue I have with certain players saying things is you always have to start with the man in the mirror before you start coming out with all these comments.”

The former United captain also questioned Martinez’s standing within the dressing room, suggesting the defender should concentrate on improving his performances.

“I don’t think it will be a big falling-out – because I think we have question marks over this dressing room anyway,” he added.

“I don’t think there’s enough characters – enough men in there – but I don’t see him as a senior player at Manchester United. I see him as a centre-half who’s making lots of mistakes.”

Neville warns Martinez has undermined United team-mates

Former United defender Gary Neville was equally critical of Martinez, arguing that his comments could cause problems within the dressing room.

Neville compared the situation to Wayne Rooney’s contract dispute in 2010, when the striker publicly questioned United’s ambition before eventually signing a new five-year deal.

“I’ve got a problem with this from a player’s perspective,” Neville said.

“That is a direct attack on the players you are playing with.

“So if I were Harry Maguire or Bruno Fernandes, or any other senior player, I would be absolutely fuming with him because you’re basically saying we shouldn’t be here and we should be bringing more players in.”

articles.content:
Fantasy Premier League 2026/27 : Bruno Fernandes among five players to either sell or avoid in Gameweek 7

It has been a disappointing start to the season for Bruno Fernandes and we recommend you dump the Manchester United captain from your Fantasy Premier League squad

Last Update:

Gameweek 7 is almost here, and there are a few popular Fantasy Premier League picks giving managers plenty to think about. Injuries have complicated things for several players, while others are struggling to justify their price tags or face a difficult run of fixtures.

Here are five players I’d consider moving on or avoiding ahead of Saturday’s deadline.

Bruno Fernandes

Price: 11.9mOwnership: 34.3%%Position: MidfielderOpponent: LEE (A), BOU (A), CHE (A)

At 11.9m, Fernandes needs to be doing more than teasing the odd haul. His 23-point explosion in Gameweek 2 accounts for most of his 32 points, with two points or fewer in the other five matches. Manchester United have scored nine goals in six league games and, while Bruno still takes penalties and creates chances, his price makes every blank expensive. Leeds away and Bournemouth at home aren’t fixtures to fear, which is why this isn’t an emergency sale if you have bigger problems. But if moving him on lets you afford Bukayo Saka or improve two other positions, I’d take the money.

Kevin Schade

Price: 6.2mOwnership: 15.0%Position: MidfielderOpponent: LIV (H), HUL (A), NFO (H)

Schade was one of the more appealing mid-priced midfielders a week ago, but an injury can change the picture pretty quickly. He hurt his shoulder against Aston Villa and came off early in the second half, with Brentford boss Keith Andrews unable to say how serious it was afterwards. Liverpool at home is next, hardly the fixture you’d choose for a player who may not be fully fit. Hull away in Gameweek 8 is much better, so there’s a case for waiting if Friday’s news is encouraging. If he’s ruled out for more than a week, though, 6.2m is too much to leave sitting there.

James Tarkowski

Price: 6.2mOwnership: 18.4%Position: DefenderOpponent: CHE (H), ARS (A), NEW (A)

Tarkowski has been a brilliant pick so far, which is exactly why I’m wary of buying him now. He’s already collected eight defensive contribution points, and Everton have kept three clean sheets in six games. That gives him a decent floor, even when the attacking returns dry up. The trouble is what comes next: Chelsea at home, Arsenal away and Newcastle away. Everton conceded twice at Hull last weekend, and it’s hard to see clean sheets coming easily against that trio. At 6.2m, I’d rather spend the money on a defender with a kinder run. Existing owners don’t necessarily need to rush him out.

Yoane Wissa

Price: 6.3mOwnership: 17.8%Position: ForwardOpponent: AVL (H), CRYI (A), EVE (H)

Newcastle’s fixture list looks reasonable on paper, but Wissa hasn’t been giving managers much back for their money. He has one goal and one assist in six league matches, with just four FPL points from his last three outings. The interesting bit is his 2.50 xG: the chances have been there, so this isn’t a striker who has stopped getting into the box. Still, Newcastle have struggled for consistency and Aston Villa, Crystal Palace and Everton won’t simply roll over. With Gonzalo García and other similarly priced forwards offering more attractive short-term fixtures, Wissa is one I’d move on if you have a spare transfer.

Cody Gakpo

Price: 7.1mOwnership: 7.6%Position: MidfielderOpponent: BRE (A), BHA (H), ARS (H)

Liverpool have enough attacking uncertainty without carrying a 7.1m midfielder who might not play. Gakpo picked up an ankle injury on international duty, missed the Manchester City game and wasn’t part of the squad for Wednesday’s European trip to LASK. There hasn’t been a firm return date, so Brentford away is a difficult fixture to plan around. Liverpool then host Brighton and Arsenal, and the emergence of other attacking options adds another question mark over his minutes once fit.

articles.summary: Rayan Cherki and Josko Gvardiol are among a quintet of players you need in your Fantasy Premier League squad
articles.content:
Fantasy Premier League 2026/27 : Manchester City duo headline five players to consider ahead of Gameweek 7

Rayan Cherki and Josko Gvardiol are among a quintet of players you need in your Fantasy Premier League squad

Last Update:

Gameweek Six in Fantasy Premier League delivered plenty of surprises, and with another round of fixtures approaching, there are some interesting players worth considering. Manchester City’s home meeting with Ipswich looks particularly appealing, while a couple of cheaper forwards could reward managers willing to look beyond the usual names.

Here are five players I’d consider bringing in this week.

Rayan Cherki

Price: 7.9mOwnership  32.2%Position: MidfielderOpponent: IPS (H), AVL (A), BHA (H)

It feels daft to spend 15.6m on Haaland and ignore the other City player causing problems. Cherki has four goals and two assists in just 392 league minutes, and nobody in City’s midfield has managed more than his 14 shots or 14 chances created. Ipswich arrive at the Etihad without a clean sheet and rank among the league’s worst sides for expected goals conceded. The worry is the team sheet. Cherki played against PSG in midweek and Foden is back, so Maresca has options. Still, if he starts, 7.9m looks a decent price for this fixture.

Gonzalo Garcia

Price: 6.1mOwnership: 7.2%Position:  ForwardOpponent: HUL (H), COV (A), AVL (A)

Garcia has scored once in six matches, which doesn’t sound particularly exciting for a striker. His 3.0 xG tell a different story. He’s started every league match, keeps getting chances in the box and now has Hull at home followed by Coventry away. Fulham have been poor, and Saturday’s late defeat at Ipswich won’t have helped confidence, but they’ve created considerably more than their goal tally suggests. Hull have made a better start than some expected, so this isn’t a guaranteed return. For managers shopping around 6m, though, Garcia offers minutes, chances and two fixtures worth attacking.

Joško Gvardiol

Price: 5.8mOwnership: 28.1%Position: DefenderOpponent : IPS (H), AVL (A), BHA (H)

It hasn’t been plain sailing for Gvardiol, yet he’s still managed 41 FPL points in six Gameweeks. That tells you why he interests me more than a defender who needs his team to keep a zero. City host Ipswich this weekend before facing Villa, Brighton, Forest and Fulham, so there is a decent run to work with rather than just one soft opponent. Gvadiol is 5.8m, he’s not cheap, and his attacking returns have come from relatively few opportunities. He’s also played 458 of a possible 540 minutes, which makes rotation the catch. I’d still back the fixture.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin

Price: 6.0mOwnership: 22.6% Position: ForwardOpponent: MUN (H), SUN (A), BOU (A)

Calvert-Lewin has been sold by plenty of managers, but Leeds’ fixture list is about to give them a reason to reconsider. The striker has had six big chances in six games, putting him among the league’s most regularly supplied forwards. Manchester United come to Elland Road without a clean sheet this season, and Sunderland and Bournemouth follow. Both have conceded 12 or more goals already. He isn’t the sort of forward you buy expecting two goals every Saturday, and Leeds won’t dominate every game. But at 6.0m, those chances and the next few opponents make him a reasonable gamble.

Marcus Tavernier

Price: 6.1mOwnership: 7.3%Position: MidfielderOpponent: SUN (H), MUN (A), LEE (H)

Bournemouth were well beaten by Chelsea last weekend, so this might feel an odd time to buy one of their players. Tavernier is still worth a look. He’s scored three times this season, has been involved in Bournemouth’s better attacking moves and can pick up points from set pieces as well as open play. Sunderland come to the Vitality Stadium having conceded 12 goals in six league matches, with Leeds at home and Ipswich away also on the horizon. The Manchester United trip in between isn’t ideal. At 6.1m, I’d rather take that fixture run than write him off because of one poor team performance.

articles.title: Lionel Messi and Inter Miami are good for each other, says Gonzalez, as champions secure play-off spot
articles.summary: Lionel Messi is heading to the MLS play-offs once again after Inter Miami enjoyed a routine win over New York City on Wednesday night
articles.content:
Lionel Messi and Inter Miami are good for each other, says Gonzalez, as champions secure play-off spot

Lionel Messi is heading to the MLS play-offs once again after Inter Miami enjoyed a routine win over New York City on Wednesday night

Last Update:

Kily Gonzalez believes Inter Miami and Lionel Messi are a perfect fit after the Argentine played a key role in the club securing their place in the MLS playoffs last night.

Messi created the second goal for former international team-mate Rodrigo De Paul, adding to German Berterame’s opener, as Miami beat New York City FC 2-0 at Nu Stadium. Miami goalkeeper Dayne St Clair preserved a clean sheet by saving Nicolas Fernandez’s penalty in the seventh minute of stoppage time.

The defending MLS champions have now locked up a top-seven finish with five games to go as they look to become the first team to defend the crown since the 2011-12 Los Angeles Galaxy.

Messi’s assist was his 14th of the season, an MLS best along with his 23 goals.

“This is a club that looks after him and protects him,” González said of Messi, who last week played his final game for his country on an emotional night in Buenos Aires.

“His team-mates show him constant affection. They go all out for him and give everything they have. He pushes us to be better every single day and challenges us.”

Gonzalez making his mark in Miami

It was also a landmark night for Berterame, who netted his first goal since May, as Miami secured their second win under Gonzalez after he took over in September from Guillermo Hoyos.

“When you have players who are willing to buy into the vision you’re trying to implement, everything becomes easier,” González added. “We recognise the mistakes we’ve been making, or are still making, and we address them during training. And really, that willingness makes it much easier to convey clear concepts.”

It has not been a straightforward season for Miami but they will enter the post-season as one of the favourites. They now sit second in the Eastern Conference but still a whopping 14 points behind runaway leaders SC Nashville.

Next up for Miami is a trip to Atlanta United on Saturday night.

Tip of the Day: Sunderland, AZ and Benfica to thrive in Europa League

We've identified a three-leg acca that we feel will take our record this week to four from four! Thursday's Tip of the Day is here...

Last Update:

It’s easy this tipping lark! Our Wednesday Tip of the Day came in and we are now three from three this week.

Tonight, we turn our attention to the Europa League and a competition in which there is a huge disparity in the quality of the teams.

We’ve identified a three-leg acca with teams to win and over one goal in the contest.

The first is Sunderland’s trip to Portugal to face Torreense. The hosts provided one of the biggest shocks in European football last season by claiming the Portuguese Cup in shades of the Wearsiders’ 1973 FA Cup triumph. But the fact remains they are a lower-ranked second division club and have won one league game in seven this season.

Sunderland have not set the world alight in the Premier League so far but they should be too good in this one.

The second is AZ Alkmaar to cruise past Hapoel Beer Sheva. AZ showed at the Stadium of Light last month what a good side they are. They suffered their first Eredivisie defeat of the season at the weekend, going down 2-0 to title rivals Feyenoord, but they should get back on track against a side that sits fourth in the Israeli First Division.

And finally, we are going for Benfica to see off Celtic.

Lisbon may be one of Celtic’s favourite European cities given it was the venue of their 1967 European Cup success but it is unlikely to be a happy return.

Martin O’Neill’s men lost three games on the bounce prior to the international break but did beat Motherwell at the weekend to quieten the noise around their manager.

But Benfica are a very different beast. Now under former Fulham boss Marco Silva, they have won nine of their last 10 in all competitions and flexed their muscles with a 2-0 victory at AC Milan in their Europa League opener.

articles.summary: Cassano does not view the Portugal star as comparable to the Brazil legend.
articles.content:
Cristiano ‘not the real Ronaldo’ – Cassano slams Portugal star

Cassano does not view the Portugal star as comparable to the Brazil legend.

Last Update:

Antonio Cassano has sharply criticised Cristiano Ronaldo, stating that he is not even “half of half” of his Brazilian namesake.

Ronaldo dominated the headlines during the recent international break, his dispute with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus  leading to him exiting their camp early and resulting in his suspension by the Portuguese Football Federation after disciplinary proceedings were opened.

The former Real Madrid and Manchester United star put the saga behind him by finding the net for Al-Nassr in their win over Diriyah.

That goal took him to 981 for his hugely decorated career. However, Cassano, who played with Brazil superstar Ronaldo during his time with Madrid, does not feel Portugal’s record goalscorer has anywhere close to the same quality.

In an interview with AS ahead of Madrid’s Champions League clash with Roma, another of Cassano’s former teams, the former Italy forward was asked about his admiration for Azzurri legend Francesco Totti.

Cassano replied: “He was one of my great idols. When I had the chance to sign for Roma or Juventus, I decided to go to Rome because that’s where Francesco had played.

“Then I had the good fortune to play alongside Ronaldo Nazário. As a centre forward, I’ve never seen anyone like him. He was absolutely fabulous and could change a game like no one else.

“If he had had a career without injuries, he would have reached an unimaginable level. That was the real Ronaldo, not Cristiano, who is half of half of Ronnie the Phenomenon.”

articles.title: Manchester United: Don’t blame Carrick, Wilcox, or even Ratcliffe. The Glazers remain the root of the problem
articles.summary: Manchester United will continue to wander aimlessly until the Glazers are gone
articles.content:
Manchester United: Don’t blame Carrick, Wilcox, or even Ratcliffe. The Glazers remain the root of the problem

Manchester United will continue to wander aimlessly until the Glazers are gone

Last Update:

The dynamic on the journey back from Madrid to Manchester must have been fascinating: the suits on one side of the departure lounge, the players on the other and Michael Carrick floating in between the two.

The chasm between the Manchester United hierarchy and everyone else at the club has been clear to see for some time. But it was brought into plain sight last night at the Metropolitano with defender Lisandro Martinez launching an astonishing attack on the owners and non-playing staff with director of football Jason Wilcox singled out.

Martinez’s gripe was that the club did not invest heavily enough over the summer, squandering the opportunity to build on their return to the Champions League.

United had a net spend of £101million in the last transfer window, eighth highest in the Premier League and lower than all three promoted clubs.

Carlos Baleba, Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans arrived, all three central midfielders. It meant the squad went into the season with one left-back and one number nine, both of whom are currently injured.

United struggle after lacklustre window

It seemed at the time they had not invested wisely and that has been proven with United 13th in the Premier League with one win from six games.

Martinez’s outburst did not come from nowhere. The Argentina international is not a regular in front of the media and he was an odd choice to be put up before the cameras. Whether he volunteered is not clear but it seems doubtful his views were his alone.

More than likely, he was speaking on behalf of a squad frustrated by a lack of progress under Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer family. Billionaire Ratcliffe’s arrival at Old Trafford in 2024 was supposed to herald a new period of spending.

And yet, if anything, it has gone the other way. Ratcliffe has embarked on a series of severe cost-cutting measures with a raft of redundancies to non-playing staff, alienated fans with some dreadful PR around ticketing, and failed to invest in an under-manned squad.

It is difficult to understand Ratcliffe’s strategy. For all his claims of being a boyhood United fan, he is first and foremost a businessman and will be eager to see a handsome return on his £1.25billion investment. For that to happen, United have to be playing Champions League football on an annual basis, increasing revenues and putting the club on a solid footing before they move into their new stadium.

But United are miles off challenging the elite in England and another top-five finish this season looks pretty unlikely at this, admittedly, early stage.

Martinez bolsters under-pressure United boss Carrick

For that to happen, Carrick has to work another miracle.

It might be that Martinez’s support – he said the former United midfielder should be backed rather than barracked – will help galvanise the dressing room in a show of solidarity. It’s undoubtedly what Carrick needs right now.

And while his tactics are often questionable, and his unassuming demeanour appears at odds with a manager aspiring to move into the elite bracket, Carrick is not the guilty party here. You could even argue Wilcox has been hung out to dry.

The blame as it has been for the past 23 years, ever since they carved their first slice of the United cake, lies with the Glazers. Invisible owners watching from afar as the club burns.

Their leveraged buyout in 2005 thrust United into a debt that still stands at over £1bn. And while that is not necessarily linked to the modest outlay on players, it is an indication of a lack of care, a lack of understanding and a lack of a coherent plan.

Ratcliffe, who owns almost 29% through his petrochemical company INEOS, is not blameless but the Glazers remain the fundamental problem with everything wrong with Manchester United.

The fish rots from the head down.

articles.title: Real Madrid: Cassano offers withering assessment of Vinicius and Mourinho
articles.summary: Cassano believes Vinicius has nothing to fall back on if he is not at his physical peak.
articles.content:
Real Madrid: Cassano offers withering assessment of Vinicius and Mourinho

Cassano believes Vinicius has nothing to fall back on if he is not at his physical peak.

Last Update:

Former Real Madrid forward Antonio Cassano has offered a scathing assessment of Vinicius Junior, claiming team-mate Rodrygo is a superior player.

Madrid continue their Champions League campaign on Wednesday as they visit the Stadio Olimpico to take on Roma in a meeting of two sides for whom Cassano played in his 18-year professional career.

Speaking to AS ahead of the game, Cassano was asked for his opinion on Vinicius, who continues to be a polarising figure in Madrid despite him scoring 129 goals in his time at the club and helping Los Blancos to three LaLiga titles and two Champions League crowns.

And Cassano is among those unimpressed by the Brazil forward.

“Vinicius is just a good player. I think Rodrygo is much better,” Cassano said in a wide-ranging interview.

“I don’t know why people talk about Vinicius so much more than his team-mate. If Vinicius isn’t physically right, he doesn’t have much else to fall back on, and he’s not particularly clinical in front of goal.

“He scores goals, but he’s not a star. I think Rodrygo, if he’s healthy, should start ahead of him. I like him much more and I’m looking forward to having him back.”

Cassano was also highly critical of Madrid boss Jose Mourinho, who returned for a second spell in charge this summer.

Madrid have made an unconvincing start under Mourinho, and sit six points behind unbeaten Barcelona in LaLiga.

Asked about the clash between Mourinho’s Madrid and a Roma side led by Gian Piero Gasperini, Cassano made it clear he has very contrasting views on the two coaches.

“Roma and Real Madrid are two very different teams. For starters, Roma has a fantastic coach and Real Madrid doesn’t because Mourinho doesn’t like to play football, he only likes to talk,” said Cassano.

“It’s incredible that Real Madrid, the greatest team in history, signed Mourinho. I don’t understand how Florentino [Perez] chose him. It drives me crazy.

“If we switched the coaches and Gasperini were on Real Madrid’s bench, Madrid would win 10-0.

“Gasperini has only won one Europa League, but I don’t care about trophies, I care about what I see on the field.

“Mourinho shouldn’t be coaching anymore. He’s been very lucky because none of his teams played well. His style of football expired 10 years ago.

“His career has left no legacy, only fights with everyone. He likes to talk about other things, but not football. One of his great advantages is having Jorge Mendes as his agent, because he always finds him good teams.”

articles.title: Arsenal have ‘a different challenge’ this season says Eze
articles.summary: The Gunners are targeting Champions League glory once more
articles.content:
Arsenal have ‘a different challenge’ this season says Eze

The Gunners are targeting Champions League glory once more

Last Update:

Arsenal midfielder Eberechi Eze says the Gunners face ‘a different challenge’ this season after finally winning the Premier League.

Mikel Arteta delivered the title in May and also steered the Gunners to the Champions League final.

Eze was on target in a 3-0 win over Lille which continued their impressive form. And the former Crystal Palace man acknowledged that the goalposts have moved now at the Emirates.

He said: “It’s now a different challenge we have. We achieved something amazing last season and we want to build on that.

“We’re coming at it at a slightly different angle but the mentality is still the same – to be ruthless and dominate as much as we can.

“It is difficult, every player wants to play. The mentality is always to be on the pitch, affect games and earn your place. I’m doing what I can, enjoying what I’m doing.

“I am always happy to score, to affect games and be having fun on the pitch and expressing myself.”

There were just seven minutes and 18 seconds between Jurriën Timber giving Arsenal the lead and Bukayo Saka making it 3-0.

The Gunners have so much strength in depth that Arteta must be aiming for that Champions League trophy this time around.

“It’s difficult in the Champions League – Lille are a brilliant team,” Arteta said.

“But winning helps – the energy will be good when we start to prepare the Sunday game.”

articles.title: Netflix secures exclusive 2030 World Cup broadcasting rights in landmark FIFA deal
articles.summary: Netflix will be broadcasting the World Cup in 2030.
articles.content:
Netflix secures exclusive 2030 World Cup broadcasting rights in landmark FIFA deal

Netflix will be broadcasting the World Cup in 2030.

Last Update:

Netflix has secured the exclusive broadcasting rights to the 2030 World Cup in Spain, marking the streaming giant’s first major agreement to show the men’s tournament.

The platform will stream all 104 matches live during the competition, which will be hosted primarily by Spain, Portugal and Morocco.

However, selected fixtures will remain available on free-to-air television, including every Spain match, both semi-finals and the final.

Netflix confirmed the agreement on Tuesday, securing the Spanish rights to the 48-team tournament.

It follows the company’s previous deal with FIFA to broadcast the Women’s World Cup in the United States in 2027 and 2031.

“As part of the agreement, one match per matchday will be available for free in Spain,” the company said in a statement.

“A package of matches, including every Spain match, both semifinals and the final, will be made available for broadcast on a national free-to-air broadcaster.”

2030 World Cup to make history across three continents

The 2030 World Cup will mark the 100th anniversary of the inaugural tournament, which was held in Uruguay in 1930.

To celebrate the centenary, FIFA has arranged for matches to take place across six countries and three continents.

Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay will each host one of the opening three fixtures before the competition moves to its main host nations of Spain, Portugal and Morocco.

Spain will enter the tournament as defending champions following their triumph at the 2026 World Cup.

Meanwhile, the battle to host the 2030 final remains unresolved, with Spain and Morocco both pushing to stage the showpiece fixture.

Real Madrid’s Santiago Bernabeu is Spain’s proposed venue, while Morocco is promoting the 115,000-capacity King Hassan II Stadium currently being built near Casablanca.

articles.title: Independent Football Regulator warns most English clubs are ‘living on financial brink’
articles.summary: The financial reality of clubs in England has been laid bare in a new report
articles.content:
Independent Football Regulator warns most English clubs are ‘living on financial brink’

The financial reality of clubs in England has been laid bare in a new report

Last Update:

The majority of English football clubs are operating under severe financial risk despite record industry revenues, according to a landmark new report from the Independent Football Regulator (IFR).

Following an 18-month investigation, the regulator’s first ‘State of the Game’ report revealed that 94% of the 160 regulated clubs are currently trading unprofitably.

Despite generating combined revenues of over £9bn, clubs across England are heavily over-reliant on owner bailouts and escalating debt to keep pace with wage inflation and rivals.

Key findings from the ‘State of the Game’ report:

“If the owner walks away, they go bust”

Speaking to Sky Sports, IFR chair David Kogan warned that English football cannot rely on endless outside investment to cover up structural failure.

He said: “We have 32 clubs that have got less than 30 days’ cash cover in their accounts. If the owner walks away or drops dead, they’re insolvent and go bust.

“Today there is enough money going through the Premier League and the EFL for the sun to shine. This is exactly the moment when we need to address structural issues, because once that sun stops shining, those clubs will be in real trouble.”

What happens next?

The regulator has put forward a six-point intervention plan ahead of introducing mandatory club licensing from November.

Under the new framework, clubs will be required to maintain at least 30 days of operating cash reserves, implement robust contingency plans for sudden ownership exits, and adopt stricter long-term debt provisions.

The IFR has also reiterated that while it prefers the Premier League and EFL to negotiate their own revamped revenue distribution deal, it retains statutory “back-stop” powers to step in and enforce a settlement if the two bodies fail to agree terms.

“These initial findings reinforce the EFL’s longstanding position that English football generates sufficient revenue to sustain both a successful Premier League and a thriving pyramid,” the EFL said.
